2ab1abcb9ca0.title: Facility Type candidate
2ab1abcb9ca0.content: Facility types are categorized following the system of health accounts through the classification of health care industries. These enable arrangement of country-specific institutions in common, internationally applicable categories. The categories are as follows: Hospitals (HP.1) Hospitals comprise licensed establishments that are primarily engaged in providing medical, diagnostic and treatment services that include physician, nursing and other health services to inpatients and the specialised accommodation services required by inpatients. Hospitals provide inpatient health services, many of which can be delivered only by using specialised facilities and professional knowledge as well as advanced medical technology and equipment, which form a significant and integral part of the provision process. Although the principal activity is the provision of inpatient medical care they may also provide day care, outpatient and home health care services. The tasks of hospitals may vary by country and are usually defined by legal requirements. In some countries, health care facilities need in addition a minimum size (such as a number of beds and medical staff to guarantee 24-hour access) in order to be registered as a hospital. Residential long-term care facilities (HP.2) The category of Residential long-term care facilities comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing residential long-term care that combines nursing, supervisory or other types of care as required by the residents. In these establishments, a significant part of the production process and the care provided is a mix of health and social services, with the health services being largely at the level of nursing care, in combination with personal care services. The medical components of care are, however, much less intensive than those provided in hospitals. Providers of ambulatory health care (HP.3) This item comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing health care services directly to outpatients who do not require inpatient services. This includes both offices of general medical practitioners and medical specialists and establishments specialising in the treatment of day-cases and in the delivery of home care services. Health practitioners in ambulatory health care primarily provide services to patients who visit the health professional’s office, or the practitioners visit the patients at home. Consequently, these establishments do not usually provide inpatient services. Ancillary services (HP.4, including transportation, emergency rescue, laboratories and others) This category comprises establishments that provide specific ancillary type of services directly to outpatients under the supervision of health professionals and not covered within the episode of treatment by hospitals, nursing care facilities, ambulatory care providers or other providers. Included are providers of patient transportation and emergency rescue, medical and diagnostic laboratories, dental laboratories and other providers of ancillary services. These specialised providers may charge patients directly for their services rendered or may provide these ancillary services as benefits-in-kind under special service contracts. Retailers (HP.5, including pharmacies) This item comprises specialised establishments whose primary activity is the retail sale of medical goods to the general public for individual or household consumption or utilisation. Establishments whose primary activity is the manufacture of medical goods, such as making lenses, orthopaedic or prosthetic appliances for direct sale to the general public for individual or household use, are also included, as is fitting and repair done in combination with sale. Note: Due to special medical safety and quality regulations, retailers of over-the-counter medical products and other providers of medical goods are subject to licensing and/or pharmaceutical authorisation in order to be eligible to provide their activities. Non-health care products such as cosmetics, dietetic products and natural products are excluded from health expenditures. Providers of preventive care (HP.6) This category comprises organisations that primarily provide collective preventive programmes and campaigns/public health programmes for specific groups of individuals or the population-at-large, such as health promotion and protection agencies or public health institutes as well as specialised establishments providing primary preventive care as their principal activity. This includes the promotion of healthy living conditions and lifestyles in schools by special outside health care professionals, agencies or organisations. Also called: Facility type . 9921374655b8.title: Public Health Workforce candidate
9921374655b8.content: The public health workforce comprises all individuals who contribute to the delivery of at least one of the essential public health functions as part of integrated services and systems. This workforce comprises diverse and multidisciplinary occupations, from the health as well as other non-health sectors. This workforce can be conceptualized as three broad groupings: core group of public health personnel who have undergone professional training and/or registration with professional bodies in public health and could be from either health or another background; health and care workers who contribute to one or more public health functions as part of their clinical and/or social care roles; and personnel from a wide group of other allied occupations who contribute to addressing the determinants of health – for instance, personnel engaged in water and sanitation, food supply chains and road safety. Also called: Public health workforce . From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 92; PDF page 106). c5ba8c8c55b1.doc: Health Workforce Education and Training Institution
c5ba8c8c55b1.title: Health Workforce Education and Training Institution candidate
c5ba8c8c55b1.content: An established institution that provides education as its main purpose, such as a school, college, university or training centre. Such institutions are normally accredited or sanctioned by the relevant national education authorities or equivalent to award qualifications. Educational institutions may also be operated by private organizations, such as religious bodies, special interest groups or private educational and training enterprises, both for-profit and not-for-profit. (108) Types of health workforce education and training institutions are: • Public: Public educational institutions provide core educational services such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres. They are controlled and managed directly by a public education authority or governing body (council, committee, etc.), the majority of whose members are appointed by a public authority. • Private: Private educational institutions provide core educational products such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres, that are controlled and directly managed either by a private organization such as a church, trade union, or business enterprise, or by a governing board whose members have mostly not been selected by a public authority. Whether or not an institution is private is therefore a matter of management, not funding. A school, for example, could in theory be entirely publicly funded but still be considered private because it is not managed by the government. In practice, for international comparability, any educational institution not managed by a government institution is classified as private. Also called: Health workforce education and training institution . From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 90; PDF page 104). 78f732149f60.title: Facility/Institution Ownership Type candidate
78f732149f60.content: Classification for ownership type: • Publicly-owned: Facilities owned or controlled by a governmental unit or a public corporation (where control is defined as the ability to determine the general corporate policy) corresponding to the institutional sector “government units” defined in the System of National Accounts 2008. • Not-for-profit privately-owned: Facilities that are legal or social entities created for the purpose of producing goods and services, whose status does not permit them to be a source of income, profit, or other financial gain for the unit(s) that establish, control or finance them, corresponding to the institutional sector “non-profit institutions serving households” defined in the System of National Accounts 2008. • For-profit privately-owned: Facilities that are legal entities set up for the purpose of producing goods and services and are capable of generating a profit or other financial gain for their owners corresponding to the institutional sector “non-financial corporations” defined in the System of National Accounts 2008. Also called: Facility/institution ownership type . From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 90; PDF page 104). eac3542e65c2.title: Remuneration candidate
eac3542e65c2.content: Average gross annual income earned by employees or those self-employed, i.e. income per year and per person, before any deductions are made for social security contributions or income tax. A person may have more than one qualifying job in any given reference period. • Income earned by employees (earnings) refers to all payments – in cash or in kind, for work done or time worked – made by their employers, and includes basic wages, overtime and other bonuses (such as for night work, work on weekends), all allowances paid by the employer (such as for working away from home or for housing) and all commissions and gratuities paid by the employer. Employers may be the government, corporations, non-profit institutions or households. • Income earned by self-employed workers refers to all payments, in cash or in kind, made by customers for goods or services, and includes capitation or fee-for-service reimbursement, bonuses, commissions, and gratuities. It should be net of operation costs/practice expenses. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 92; PDF page 106). 9f74ca35a3cd.title: Status in Employment candidate
9f74ca35a3cd.content: One of two categories of the total employed: (a) wage and salaried workers (employees): workers who hold a job defined as “paid employment”, with explicit (written or oral) or implicit employment contracts that give them a basic remuneration that is not directly dependent upon the revenue of the unit for which they work, and (b) self-employed workers: workers who, working on their own account or with one or more partners or in a cooperative, hold a “self-employment job”, i.e. one in which the remuneration is directly dependent upon the profits derived from the goods and services produced. Also called: Status in employment . From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 93; PDF page 107). bf75fe1ffabe.content: Health workers who provide health education, referral and follow-up, case management, basic preventive health care and home visiting services to specific communities. f74714413d8e.title: Place of Training candidate
f74714413d8e.content: This is defined as the place of first qualification for the health worker. Personnel may be categorized as either domestic-trained, foreign-trained, or their place of training may be unknown. The foreign-trained health personnel may also be disaggregated into “foreign-trained national-born” (people born in a country who went to study in another country but have come back afterwards to practice in their home country) and “foreign-trained foreign-born”. Also called: Place of training . From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 92; PDF page 106). bdd9433f0c51-3.title: Narrower
bdd9433f0c51-3.content: . | In a national context an electronic health workforce registry can be considered the single authoritative source of health workforce information that can provide an accurate count of all health care personnel that either have worked or are currently working at national or sub-national levels, including in the private sector. | An electronic health workforce registry can be designed to authenticate and validate the existence of a health worker and provide essential details about that person. | In addition, a health workforce registry can ensure quality control, provide easy access to information on production, distribution and utilization of health personnel, and assist in budgeting, research development and advocacy. | A health workforce registry allows aggregation of health workforce data in several combinations and assists both national and sub-national ministries of health in producing essential indicator-based reports, as needed. | The health workforce registry is a central and essential component of a functional HRIS, as it contains important health worker attributes that can subsequently be linked to other relevant HRIS components. | Address policy and governance mechanism | Agree on a location to operate the registry | Assure privacy, security and confidentiality of health workforce data | Establish standardized reports | Number of health workforce by cadre, gender and facility | Number of expected retirements | Number of expected and completed renewals of license/credentials | Number of vacant positions by facility | Geographic distribution of total workforce by facility | Geographic distribution (by district) of male and female employees | Develop, test, and deploy a functional electronic health workforce registry | Establish appropriate access controls based on an agreed policies. | Design, test and deploy the electronic web-enabled registry based on national eHealth enterprise architecture. | Make available, at sub-national level, a replica of the registry with similar structure and functions, in order to collect and manage the minimum data set from authorized entities at sub-national-level. | Adhere to best practices in information systems design to assure accuracy, timeliness, completeness, reliability, privacy, security, and confidentiality of data and information systems and assets. | Illustration depicting a web-enabled electronic Health Workforce Registry with person-centric data entry screen and analytics display abilities | Based on national or sub-national eHealth enterprise information architecture, national and sub-national health authorities shall develop and deploy the registry. | The registry shall conform to best practices in information systems design in order to assure quality, accuracy, timeliness, completeness, reliability, privacy, security, and confidentiality of the data and information systems and assets. | Legally authorized users of the registry shall be required to have unique user names and passwords that will be provided by the national Steering Committee, on the approval of the highest health authority at national and sub-national levels. Level of access to the registry shall be determined by the national Steering Committee or its authorized agent. | The registry must be in compliance with all applicable national and sub-national laws related to privacy, security, and confidentiality of data. | The registry and its related physical assets shall be secured in accordance with applicable national and sub-national laws. | .

bfe515cd20d9.title: Outcome indicators candidate
bfe515cd20d9.content: Indicators that provide insights into the tangible results for stakeholders that arise from the adoption and use of eHealth. Worldwide, the application of information and communication technologies to support national health-care services is rapidly expanding and increasingly important. This is especially so at a time when all health systems face stringent economic challenges and greater demands to provide more and better care, especially to those most in need. The National eHealth Strategy Toolkit is an expert, practical guide that provides governments, their ministries and stakeholders with a solid foundation and method for the development and implementation of a national eHealth vision, action plan and monitoring framework. All countries, whatever their level of development, can adapt the Toolkit to suit their own circumstances. Representing one of the most significant collaborations in recent years between the World Health Organization and the International Telecommunication Union, the Toolkit is a landmark in understanding what eHealth is, what it can do, and why and how it should be applied to health care today. Verbatim from the source; a candidate until an editor adopts it (glossary-from-source).

37291b5b705c.title: quality of the evidence
37291b5b705c.content: In the context of guideline development, the confidence that the estimates of an effect are adequate to support a particular decision or recommendation. Rated high, moderate, low or very low. Also called: certainty of the evidence, confidence in the estimates of effect . The WHO handbook for guideline development (2nd edition, §9.1, p. 122) names both alternatives: "Alternative terms to describe the quality of the evidence are 'certainty of the evidence' or 'confidence in the estimates of effect'." The handbook uses 'quality of the evidence' 77 times and 'certainty of the evidence' once; the who-guideline-development voice and the platform's `grade-certainty` code list use 'certainty', GRADE's later name. Rated for a body of evidence per outcome, never for a single study. Not the strength of a recommendation, which the handbook keeps apart throughout.

The handbook cites its reference 108 for this entry. | Health Workforce Education and Training Institution (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))An established institution that provides education as its main purpose, such as a school, college, university or training centre. Such institutions are normally accredited or sanctioned by the relevant national education authorities or equivalent to award qualifications. Educational institutions may also be operated by private organizations, such as religious bodies, special interest groups or private educational and training enterprises, both for-profit and not-for-profit. (108) Types of health workforce education and training institutions are: • Public: Public educational institutions provide core educational services such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres. They are controlled and managed directly by a public education authority or governing body (council, committee, etc.), the majority of whose members are appointed by a public authority. • Private: Private educational institutions provide core educational products such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres, that are controlled and directly managed either by a private organization such as a church, trade union, or business enterprise, or by a governing board whose members have mostly not been selected by a public authority. Whether or not an institution is private is therefore a matter of management, not funding. A school, for example, could in theory be entirely publicly funded but still be considered private because it is not managed by the government. Facility Type candidate Facility types are categorized following the system of health accounts through the classification of health care industries. These enable arrangement of country-specific institutions in common, internationally applicable categories. The categories are as follows: Hospitals (HP.1) Hospitals comprise licensed establishments that are primarily engaged in providing medical, diagnostic and treatment services that include physician, nursing and other health services to inpatients and the specialised accommodation services required by inpatients. Hospitals provide inpatient health services, many of which can be delivered only by using specialised facilities and professional knowledge as well as advanced medical technology and equipment, which form a significant and integral part of the provision process. Although the principal activity is the provision of inpatient medical care they may also provide day care, outpatient and home health care services. The tasks of hospitals may vary by country and are usually defined by legal requirements. In some countries, health care facilities need in addition a minimum size (such as a number of beds and medical staff to guarantee 24-hour access) in order to be registered as a hospital. Residential long-term care facilities (HP.2) The category of Residential long-term care facilities comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing residential long-term care that combines nursing, supervisory or other types of care as required by the residents. In these establishments, a significant part of the production process and the care provided is a mix of health and social services, with the health services being largely at the level of nursing care, in combination with personal care services. The medical components of care are, however, much less intensive than those provided in hospitals. Providers of ambulatory health care (HP.3) This item comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing health care services directly to outpatients who do not require inpatient services. This includes both offices of general medical practitioners and medical specialists and establishments specialising in the treatment of day-cases and in the delivery of home care services. Health practitioners in ambulatory health care primarily provide services to patients who visit the health professional’s office, or the practitioners visit the patients at home. Consequently, these establishments do not usually provide inpatient services. Ancillary services (HP.4, including transportation, emergency rescue, laboratories and others) This category comprises establishments that provide specific ancillary type of services directly to outpatients under the supervision of health professionals and not covered within the episode of treatment by hospitals, nursing care facilities, ambulatory care providers or other providers. Included are providers of patient transportation and emergency rescue, medical and diagnostic laboratories, dental laboratories and other providers of ancillary services. These specialised providers may charge patients directly for their services rendered or may provide these ancillary services as benefits-in-kind under special service contracts. Retailers (HP.5, including pharmacies) This item comprises specialised establishments whose primary activity is the retail sale of medical goods to the general public for individual or household consumption or utilisation. Establishments whose primary activity is the manufacture of medical goods, such as making lenses, orthopaedic or prosthetic appliances for direct sale to the general public for individual or household use, are also included, as is fitting and repair done in combination with sale. Note: Due to special medical safety and quality regulations, retailers of over-the-counter medical products and other providers of medical goods are subject to licensing and/or pharmaceutical authorisation in order to be eligible to provide their activities. Non-health care products such as cosmetics, dietetic products and natural products are excluded from health expenditures. Providers of preventive care (HP.6) This category comprises organisations that primarily provide collective preventive programmes and campaigns/public health programmes for specific groups of individuals or the population-at-large, such as health promotion and protection agencies or public health institutes as well as specialised establishments providing primary preventive care as their principal activity. This includes the promotion of healthy living conditions and lifestyles in schools by special outside health care professionals, agencies or organisations. 5fbe13d04fa8.content: Gender candidate Gender refers to the characteristics of women, men, girls and boys that are socially constructed. This includes norms, behaviours and roles associated with being a woman, man, girl or boy, as well as relationships with each other. As a social construct, gender varies from society to society and can change over time. Gender is hierarchical and produces inequalities that intersect with other social and economic inequalities. The handbook cites its reference 48 for this entry. | Facility Type (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))Facility types are categorized following the system of health accounts through the classification of health care industries. These enable arrangement of country-specific institutions in common, internationally applicable categories. The categories are as follows: Hospitals (HP.1) Hospitals comprise licensed establishments that are primarily engaged in providing medical, diagnostic and treatment services that include physician, nursing and other health services to inpatients and the specialised accommodation services required by inpatients. Hospitals provide inpatient health services, many of which can be delivered only by using specialised facilities and professional knowledge as well as advanced medical technology and equipment, which form a significant and integral part of the provision process. Although the principal activity is the provision of inpatient medical care they may also provide day care, outpatient and home health care services. The tasks of hospitals may vary by country and are usually defined by legal requirements. In some countries, health care facilities need in addition a minimum size (such as a number of beds and medical staff to guarantee 24-hour access) in order to be registered as a hospital. Residential long-term care facilities (HP.2) The category of Residential long-term care facilities comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing residential long-term care that combines nursing, supervisory or other types of care as required by the residents. In these establishments, a significant part of the production process and the care provided is a mix of health and social services, with the health services being largely at the level of nursing care, in combination with personal care services. The medical components of care are, however, much less intensive than those provided in hospitals. Providers of ambulatory health care (HP.3) This item comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing health care services directly to outpatients who do not require inpatient services. This includes both offices of general medical practitioners and medical specialists and establishments specialising in the treatment of day-cases and in the delivery of home care services. Health practitioners in ambulatory health care primarily provide services to patients who visit the health professional’s office, or the practitioners visit the patients at home. Consequently, these establishments do not usually provide inpatient services. Ancillary services (HP.4, including transportation, emergency rescue, laboratories and others) This category comprises establishments that provide specific ancillary type of services directly to outpatients under the supervision of health professionals and not covered within the episode of treatment by hospitals, nursing care facilities, ambulatory care providers or other providers. Included are providers of patient transportation and emergency rescue, medical and diagnostic laboratories, dental laboratories and other providers of ancillary services. These specialised providers may charge patients directly for their services rendered or may provide these ancillary services as benefits-in-kind under special service contracts. Retailers (HP.5, including pharmacies) This item comprises specialised establishments whose primary activity is the retail sale of medical goods to the general public for individual or household consumption or utilisation. Establishments whose primary activity is the manufacture of medical goods, such as making lenses, orthopaedic or prosthetic appliances for direct sale to the general public for individual or household use, are also included, as is fitting and repair done in combination with sale. Note: Due to special medical safety and quality regulations, retailers of over-the-counter medical products and other providers of medical goods are subject to licensing and/or pharmaceutical authorisation in order to be eligible to provide their activities. Non-health care products such as cosmetics, dietetic products and natural products are excluded from health expenditures. Providers of preventive care (HP.6) This category comprises organisations that primarily provide collective preventive programmes and campaigns/public health programmes for specific groups of individuals or the population-at-large, such as health promotion and protection agencies or public health institutes as well as specialised establishments providing primary preventive care as their principal activity. This includes the promotion of healthy living conditions and lifestyles in schools by special outside health care professionals, agencies or organisations. (108) Types of health workforce education and training institutions are: • Public: Public educational institutions provide core educational services such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres. They are controlled and managed directly by a public education authority or governing body (council, committee, etc.), the majority of whose members are appointed by a public authority. • Private: Private educational institutions provide core educational products such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres, that are controlled and directly managed either by a private organization such as a church, trade union, or business enterprise, or by a governing board whose members have mostly not been selected by a public authority. Whether or not an institution is private is therefore a matter of management, not funding. A school, for example, could in theory be entirely publicly funded but still be considered private because it is not managed by the government. Examples for subnational administrative units are states, regions, provinces, counties, and districts. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 93; PDF page 107). The library ingest of this edition has no Glossary section, so the definition was extracted from the PDF text layer on 2026-10-31 and needs a person to confirm it. The handbook cites its reference 47 for this entry. | Active Health Worker (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))One who provides services to patients and communities (practising health worker) or whose medical education is a prerequisite for the execution of the job (e.g. education, research, public administration) even if the health worker is not directly providing services (professionally active health worker). If data are not available for practising or professionally active health workers, data with the closest definition can be used, such as “health worker licensed to practice”. Categories of level are based on the definitions of OECD/Eurostat/WHO-Europe Joint questionnaire on non-monetary health care statistics. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 88; PDF page 102). The library ingest of this edition has no Glossary section, so the definition was extracted from the PDF text layer on 2026-10-31 and needs a person to confirm it. The handbook cites its reference 48 for this entry. | Occupation (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))The concept of occupation is defined as a “set of jobs whose main tasks and duties are characterized by a high degree of similarity”. A job is defined as “a set of tasks and duties performed, or meant to be performed, by one person, including for an employer or in self-employment”. The National Health Workforce Accounts covers health and health-related occupations grouped according to the International Standard Classification of Occupations 2008. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 92; PDF page 106). The library ingest of this edition has no Glossary section, so the definition was extracted from the PDF text layer on 2026-10-31 and needs a person to confirm it. The handbook cites its reference 46 for this entry. | Remuneration (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))Average gross annual income earned by employees or those self-employed, i.e. income per year and per person, before any deductions are made for social security contributions or income tax. A person may have more than one qualifying job in any given reference period. • Income earned by employees (earnings) refers to all payments – in cash or in kind, for work done or time worked – made by their employers, and includes basic wages, overtime and other bonuses (such as for night work, work on weekends), all allowances paid by the employer (such as for working away from home or for housing) and all commissions and gratuities paid by the employer. Employers may be the government, corporations, non-profit institutions or households. • Income earned by self-employed workers refers to all payments, in cash or in kind, made by customers for goods or services, and includes capitation or fee-for-service reimbursement, bonuses, commissions, and gratuities. It should be net of operation costs/practice expenses. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 92; PDF page 106). The handbook cites its reference 58 for this entry. | Status in Employment (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))One of two categories of the total employed: (a) wage and salaried workers (employees): workers who hold a job defined as “paid employment”, with explicit (written or oral) or implicit employment contracts that give them a basic remuneration that is not directly dependent upon the revenue of the unit for which they work, and (b) self-employed workers: workers who, working on their own account or with one or more partners or in a cooperative, hold a “self-employment job”, i.e. one in which the remuneration is directly dependent upon the profits derived from the goods and services produced. This includes norms, behaviours and roles associated with being a woman, man, girl or boy, as well as relationships with each other. As a social construct, gender varies from society to society and can change over time. Gender is hierarchical and produces inequalities that intersect with other social and economic inequalities. Outcome indicators candidate Indicators that provide insights into the tangible results for stakeholders that arise from the adoption and use of eHealth. Worldwide, the application of information and communication technologies to support national health-care services is rapidly expanding and increasingly important. This is especially so at a time when all health systems face stringent economic challenges and greater demands to provide more and better care, especially to those most in need. The National eHealth Strategy Toolkit is an expert, practical guide that provides governments, their ministries and stakeholders with a solid foundation and method for the development and implementation of a national eHealth vision, action plan and monitoring framework. All countries, whatever their level of development, can adapt the Toolkit to suit their own circumstances. Representing one of the most significant collaborations in recent years between the World Health Organization and the International Telecommunication Union, the Toolkit is a landmark in understanding what eHealth is, what it can do, and why and how it should be applied to health care today. Public Health Workforce candidate The public health workforce comprises all individuals who contribute to the delivery of at least one of the essential public health functions as part of integrated services and systems. This workforce comprises diverse and multidisciplinary occupations, from the health as well as other non-health sectors. This workforce can be conceptualized as three broad groupings: core group of public health personnel who have undergone professional training and/or registration with professional bodies in public health and could be from either health or another background; health and care workers who contribute to one or more public health functions as part of their clinical and/or social care roles; and personnel from a wide group of other allied occupations who contribute to addressing the determinants of health – for instance, personnel engaged in water and sanitation, food supply chains and road safety. 4fb2ea1ce2ce.content: quality assurance QA candidate No definition yet. Verbatim from the source; a candidate until an editor adopts it (glossary-from-source). Term page · Digital transformation handbook for health supply chain architecture · https://litlfred.github.io/who-iris/v0/ns/glossary/9789240101197-eng/quality-assurance · source library/9789240101197-eng/sections/sec-001-abbreviations-and-acronyms.md#L48 . quality of the evidence In the context of guideline development, the confidence that the estimates of an effect are adequate to support a particular decision or recommendation. Rated high, moderate, low or very low. The WHO handbook for guideline development (2nd edition, §9.1, p. 122) names both alternatives: "Alternative terms to describe the quality of the evidence are 'certainty of the evidence' or 'confidence in the estimates of effect'." The handbook uses 'quality of the evidence' 77 times and 'certainty of the evidence' once; the who-guideline-development voice and the platform's `grade-certainty` code list use 'certainty', GRADE's later name. Rated for a body of evidence per outcome, never for a single study. Not the strength of a recommendation, which the handbook keeps apart throughout. Remuneration candidate Average gross annual income earned by employees or those self-employed, i.e. income per year and per person, before any deductions are made for social security contributions or income tax. A person may have more than one qualifying job in any given reference period. • Income earned by employees (earnings) refers to all payments – in cash or in kind, for work done or time worked – made by their employers, and includes basic wages, overtime and other bonuses (such as for night work, work on weekends), all allowances paid by the employer (such as for working away from home or for housing) and all commissions and gratuities paid by the employer. Employers may be the government, corporations, non-profit institutions or households. • Income earned by self-employed workers refers to all payments, in cash or in kind, made by customers for goods or services, and includes capitation or fee-for-service reimbursement, bonuses, commissions, and gratuities. It should be net of operation costs/practice expenses. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 92; PDF page 106). Vacancy Rate 1-11 candidate Ratio of unfilled posts to total number of funded posts . NHWA indicator 1 – 11. The definition is the sheet's "Indicator name"; the label is its "Abbreviated name". Numerator: "Number of funded full-time posts that have not been filled for at least twelve months". Denominator: "Total number of funded full-time posts (filled and unfilled)". Candidate definitions (4) . | Occupation (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))The concept of occupation is defined as a “set of jobs whose main tasks and duties are characterized by a high degree of similarity”. A job is defined as “a set of tasks and duties performed, or meant to be performed, by one person, including for an employer or in self-employment”. The National Health Workforce Accounts covers health and health-related occupations grouped according to the International Standard Classification of Occupations 2008. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 92; PDF page 106). 46f7db3deb43.content: activate-accepted-guidance candidate, extracted The point-of-care system carries out the health worker's decisions on decision-support guidance: each accepted action's request becomes active (intent plan or order) and joins the client's CarePlan; a declined action is not written. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/adopt-methodology-from-source.md . adversarial-code-review candidate, extracted Review a pull request an agent touched by building the strongest case that it is wrong, unsafe, or not what it claims, and record the verdict where the merge gate reads it: one merge-review/v1 file per head, on the merge-reviews state branch, never in the pull request itself. Covers who may review, what the whole-diff scope is, the RED FLAG categories and their evidence rule, the one rebuttal round, overrides, and how a per-head verdict composes with a merge train. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/adversarial-code-review.md . agent-handoff candidate, extracted Governs handing ONE task to an agent in another environment — a local agent with network the cloud session lacks, a sibling on a different machine, anything that cannot read the coordinator's context and that a person may relay to. States who writes which work item, where the receiver reports, what the person pastes (one sentence: work item, branch, repository) and the brief the work item opens with (second person, to the executor), what the receiver checks before acting, who closes, who may grant an exception, and how to recognise and answer the five ways an executor fails. Use when writing a work item for another agent to execute, and as the receiver before acting on one. Triggers on: hand off, handoff, local agent, agy, mac agent, needs network, executor failed, agent went silent, re-hand, "give me a branch and bean for them", relay, the other agent. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/agent-handoff.md . agent-memory candidate, extracted Durable memory for a subagent — the three entry labels and what each promises, why entries are authored as graph nodes rather than in the generated file, the injection budget that silently truncates, and archiving as the third state between "reaches everybody" and "deleted". Vendor-neutral: the coding agent is a Tool (Claude Code is one; Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot and Codex are others), and each Tool's own config format belongs to its adapter, not here. Covers the permissions the harness's processes need, least privilege, how each one is explained before it is granted, how a grant is recorded, and the rules that no grant relaxes: never self-granted, generated projections are CI's, and merging to main is never a standing permission. ea924c451363.content: dak-l1-library candidate, extracted Build a DAK's library from the L1 sources its Component 1 cites, and the L1 knowledge graph that records them. Read when starting or extending a DAK library, when a DAK's guidance changes, and before writing any L1 graph for a DAK. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/L1/skills/smart-l1/dak-l1-library.md . dak-postprocessing candidate, extracted What the DAK post-processing phase produces after the IG Publisher runs — the JSON/JSON-LD surface, the DAK API hub, and the metadata-to-Liquid bridge — and how an IG repository's own site gets the same sidecars from the cached AST (ig-site:sidecars). Read before changing a post-processing step, and before assuming the Publisher produced something it did not. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/L3/skills/smart-l3/dak-postprocessing.md . dak-preprocessing candidate, extracted What each DAK pre-processing step does before the IG Publisher runs, which steps exist only to feed the Publisher's page index, and how the phase runs as the overlay on fhir-harness's AST cache refresh (dak-pre-export.sh). Also which files in a DAK repository are authored and which are generated, and the SEMVER rule for DAK and IG versions. Read before changing, assuming or moving a pre-processing step. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/L3/skills/smart-l3/dak-preprocessing.md . data-modelling candidate, extracted Build a data model: identify the entities a body of work is actually about, the relations between them, and the cardinalities — then declare it where the tools can read it. Process-agnostic technique; the CRDM phase that invokes it is crdm-data-model. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/data-modelling.md . decision-audit candidate, extracted Record why a decision was made, or why a finding in it was left. Required of whoever adjudicates a gate, and of the agent that assembles the citations for them. Every overrule of a mechanical finding carries a note, and every note cites corpus evidence. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/process-core/decision-audit.md . decision-comparison candidate, extracted Lay a decision out as a comparison before you ask it — what each option does, its pro, its con, what it changes downstream, and how reversible it is — in the prose that precedes the question, never inside the option labels. Required whenever a choice is handed to a person. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/decision-comparison.md . decision-methodology-selector candidate, extracted Given a decision context, select the applicable methodology from the methodology graph. Reads the graph's applies-when declarations, matches them against the context, and returns the ranked applicable methods with rationale. Extends methodology-adoption's four-question protocol with quantitative method-selection criteria from the MCDM literature. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/process-core/decision-methodology-selector.md . deep-document-research candidate, extracted Answer a question from a corpus this folio already holds, iteratively, and stop on a stated condition. The four roles, the two stopping conditions and why both are load-bearing, the granularity choice, and the three things this repository must NOT adopt along with the method. Skills of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/skills/deep-document-research.md . definition-clarity-audit candidate, extracted Definition / statement clarity + concision audit. A content block can validate (schema-clean, refs resolve, formal-proof sibling present) and still read badly: the defined term is never emphasised, the definition is buried under paragraphs of motivation, or one definition block silently bundles three or four distinct definienda. Use when asked to "bold defined terms", "tighten definitions", "no rambling definitions", "one definition per block", "tight theorem/proposition/lemma statements", or to set up / run a clarity audit. 90d4deb913c3.content: hand-back-to-discussion candidate, extracted A sibling agent, spawned during or working beside a live agent-human discussion, hands every card, question, decision, result, blocker or piece of context back to the discussion agent that is talking with the person, and never leaves it only in its own thread. The discussion agent asks the person (ask-the-person), marks every copy answered, and routes the answer back. A review sheet or issue in play is an extra channel. Use whenever an agent that is not the one talking with the person has something the person must see. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/hand-back-to-discussion.md . handover-report candidate, extracted Write a handover report: a templated snapshot of an agent's current state, committed as a work item note, so that a session or subagent that stalls, runs out of context, or loses its container can be picked up by another agent without re-deriving anything. Use it when you are told a stall is likely, at the end of every long arc, before a risky or long-running step, and whenever a steward asks for one. Its reader is stalled-agent-triage. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/handover-report.md . harness-projections candidate, extracted Who may write under .claude/, and when. The generated projections of the knowledge graph (.claude/commands/*.md from skill:commands, the assembled agent memory under .claude/agents/ and .claude/agent-memory/) are written by CI, which commits them to the PR branch, and never by an agent. A hand-edited .claude/ file (settings.json, its hooks, a hand-written command or agent definition) changes only with the owner's explicit consent to that change: the agent shows the exact diff and the reason, asks first, and records the consent. Read before staging any path under .claude/. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/harness-projections.md . harness-requirements candidate, extracted What a layer OWES for every directory it declares — a visualiser, a documentation entry, a governing skill, json/jsonld/schema.json serialisations at the directory's URL and at every node beneath it, and a starting README of its own. Read before declaring a directory, before adding a graph typology, and when reading check:subgraph-coverage. Carries which obligations are ranked as unmet promises rather than unanswered questions, why the discriminator is "is this the static knowledge graph", and which single obligation a harness may never waive. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/harness-requirements.md . harness-tiles candidate, extracted A tile is a function of the harness watching a directory, not of nodes. Where the tile set comes from, what a tile opens, and the two gaps it reports rather than hides. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/ui/ui-core/harness-tiles.md . html-rendering-qc candidate, extracted Check that a folio's content blocks render correctly as HTML on its published site, and report each defect with its source file and line. The generic half: what the HTML path is, which patterns break it, and how to look at the result. A content type adds its own rows through a refinement skill. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/platform-ui/skills/platform-ui/html-rendering-qc.md . human-agent-discussion candidate, extracted Ask a person (or a sibling agent) for what no file holds. First determine where you are — the context, the Role you act as and theirs, the Process and task (or that you are idle) — and ask about whichever you cannot determine before anything else. Then context, the options, a recommendation and what happens with no answer, then ONE question. Skills of bootstrap · source bootstrap/skills/human-agent-discussion.md . hypothesis-generation candidate, extracted Formulate evidence-bounded scientific questions, candidate hypotheses, rival explanations, causal or associational claims, discriminating predictions, measurements, and preregistration-ready analysis plans. Use when turning observations or preliminary findings into transparent, testable research plans without treating hypotheses as facts. Skills of folio-assistant-sci · source folio-assistant-sci/skills/content/hypothesis-generation/hypothesis-generation.md .

Read when an IG site build refuses with "injection QA", when asked to review an IG's content for injection, or before changing the gate, its pattern rules or the browser's check in ast-resource.js. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-content-qa.md . ig-publication candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/content/fhir-ig-authoring/ig-publication.md . ig-publisher-fork candidate, extracted Requirements for an agent working a local experimental fork of the IG Publisher — which repositories, what the AST must carry, what must not change, and the acceptance criteria. Read before forking, and before reporting a fork's work complete. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-publisher-fork.md . ig-publisher-reduction candidate, extracted The phased transition that reduces the IG Publisher to AST + QA — five phases, each with an exit criterion that is measured rather than asserted, and the staleness contract that makes an AST-backed staging build honest. Read before starting any phase, and before claiming one is done. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-publisher-reduction.md . ig-publisher-service-contract candidate, extracted The contract the ig-publisher-service role is held to: what the JVM services an IG build shells out to must produce, and how a caller tells a pass from a run that never happened. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/content/fhir-ig-authoring/ig-publisher-service-contract.md . ig-render-jekyll candidate, extracted Rendering a FHIR IG's content through the just-the-docs pipeline instead of mounting the IG Publisher's finished HTML — the JSON-only representation contract, navigation derived from sushi-config.yaml, and the LHS rail. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-render-jekyll.md . ig-site-links candidate, extracted What happens to an IG's links when its pages are rendered on our site rather than by the IG Publisher: which are rewritten (artefact pages, a case-only mismatch, the Publisher's downloads and pages, files of the IG's repository, the OpenAPI index), which are reported as the IG's own dead links, and the gate that keeps a generator from linking a page it does not write. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-site-links.md . ig-site-theme candidate, extracted How an IG rendered through just-the-docs wears the theme its instance ALREADY declares: the one webpage theme becomes the IG site's colour scheme. Read before theming an IG site, adding a theme to an IG instance, or concluding that a staged IG is unthemed. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-site-theme.md . incremental-render candidate, extracted Rendering only what changed — seeding a build from a previous render, the two edges that decide what must re-run, why a step declares GRAPH TYPOLOGIES rather than paths, and the rule that could-not-determine always re-renders rather than serving a stale page. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/platform-ui/skills/platform-ui/incremental-render.md . index-config candidate, extracted index.config.json at an instantiation root says which harnesses the checkout instantiates, where each one comes from (local, or a remote mount pinned to a SHA), each layer's config INLINE in its entry (a legacy <name>.config.json is only imported until --inline retires it), and which harness / is. Covers instantiated against declared, landing resolution and its error case, index.lock.json and its legacy fallback, the reserved index stem, the generated .gitignore block and its gate, and index-config:migrate (with --inline) for separated repositories. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/index-config.md . indicator-extraction candidate, extracted Extract the indicators an L1 source prints (indicator reference or metadata sheets: name, numerator, denominator, disaggregation, definition, data sources) as L1 indicator nodes with every printed field, then draft one L2 program indicator per indicator, derived from its L1 node. Read before adding a WHO handbook's or guideline's indicators to a DAK or a DTH, and whenever an L2 indicator has to trace to its source. Part of L1 → L2 extraction for every DAK and DTH, beside recommendation-extraction. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/L1/skills/smart-l1/indicator-extraction.md . inform-client candidate, extracted A health worker tells the client (or caregiver) what was decided and what happens next, in words and, where the DAK gives one, on a slip or card: a referral, a return date, a result. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/L4/skills/smart-l4/inform-client.md . initialization-steps candidate, extracted Walk every initialization step the declarations name (the layer's own and each one it needs), check each before doing anything, do what can be done, ask for what only a person can do, and report every step as done, not done, could not determine, or stated. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/security/injection-boundaries.md . instance-kinds candidate, extracted How to make a new KIND of harness layer — choosing the prefix family, the keep-the-kind's-name default and the owner's right to decline it, which inherited files the new owner may repoint, and what a new GRAPH typology must declare. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/instance-publication.md . integration-audit candidate, extracted Sidecar-invalidation utility for the integration-watcher pipeline. Adds mechanical QA fields (script-reviewer entries) to per-block .qa.json sidecars and marks the existing entries stale so the next qa-sweep re-evaluates them. Use when a checker bug is fixed in a QA checker module (downstream "fresh" entries are now incorrect) or when a registry update adds a criterion the block hasn't been audited under. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/editorial/skills/editorial-audits/integration-audit.md . integration-backlog candidate, extracted Dispatcher for the /integration-backlog <axes> slash command. Works the backlog identified by the integration watchers (proof, canonical, compute, detangler, one-voice, …) by clustering the open findings into review-sized batches (≤ 49 files per PR — the reviewer-bot limit), proposing each batch to the author via structured AskUserQuestion calls, running /prepare-merge on each, resolving review comments (auto if mechanical, structured AskUserQuestion if architectural), then merging — and repeating until the axis is exhausted or the author signals stop. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/integration-watch.md . integration-watcher candidate, extracted Abstract parent skill for domain-specific **integration watchers**. Encodes the shared mechanics — Monitor on origin/main, PR subscriptions, per-event QA dispatch, queue + ledger, idle backlog sweep, idle author-ask dispatcher, watch-PRs-you-prepare protocol, voice-pass on PR diff, witness-drift CI recovery, billing-quick-fail flake handling — that every concrete watcher inherits. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/integration-watcher.md . interaction-modality candidate, extracted Establish how to talk to the person in front of you before deciding what to say — audio, ordinary chat, selectable options for limited hand function, large-type for low vision, plain language — and hold that choice durably so every later session and sibling agent honours it. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/interaction-modality.md . iris-cdn-exporter candidate, extracted The IRIS CDN Exporter agent — how WHO IRIS is exported onto Cloudflare — a git repository on Cloudflare Artifacts and R2 behind the CDN — with an initial load (metadata and PDFs), a nightly change ingest over the DSpace REST API, a weekly reconciliation, and one signed release per run. Skills of who-iris · source who-iris/skills/iris-rest-feed.md . issue-working candidate, extracted Working a tracked issue — announce the branch when you create it rather than when you finish, and re-check the issue for new AND edited comments while you work. 6fbc26adf874.content: journey-maps candidate, extracted Journeys and workshops as knowledge-graph content: a DAK user scenario told as a journey map (user-scenario kind: ordered steps, per person what they do and feel, pain points, enablers, the record's trust state, and edges to stories, BPMN tasks, requirements, FHIR examples, building blocks and the DAK's data sets, decision tables and indicators), the building-blocks catalogue its steps use, a workshop that teaches from it (workshop kind: modules, objectives, questions for the room on each step, reference tables, sheets, job aids), the journeys-viewer visualiser that draws them for a layer and the layers it mounts, and the check:journey-refs gate that every reference they name resolves. c454425edb02.content: Edit deterministic logic (if needed) candidate, extracted If the content change affects decision logic, indicators, or workflows: - Update CQL expressions - Update DMN decision tables - Adjust indicator definitions skill: dak-authoring, fhir-pipeline . Edit it in place — it is your own content candidate, extracted The ordinary path, drawn so the process does not read as though every edit needs a copy. Content in a writable directory is authored content and is edited where it lives; the copy-out is for somebody else's bytes, not for yours. Edit the component candidate, extracted Create or change the component with the authoring skill the call names, one component per pass. On rework, apply the review's findings; a fix written in an AuditNote is applied as given. An adapted component is edited against its pinned upstream, so the before side of the diff is that upstream, not an empty file. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/L2/collab/processes/l2-component-edit-review.bpmn#Task_Edit . Edit the document as decided, on a feature branch candidate, extracted public-comment edit --branch: the author (human, or an agent in the author role) edits the folio's blocks as the decision says, on a feature branch for one change-set. Its PR says Closes #N for the change-set issue, and opening it moves that issue's accepted comments to editing. Before its preview is staged, the author writes the change set's Disposition (change set) on the Agent tab: one line per comment (No. 136: Accepted...), starting from each comment's Blue Disposition on Review Public Comments, after an optional Overall statement. Quality check: every comment number in the change set has a disposition; the sheet flags gaps and words that differ from the people's. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/public-comment-change.bpmn#Task_AuthorEdits . Edit the document in the row's pull request candidate, extracted One row, one branch, one active pull request: the agent edits on the row's branch and opens its pull request, or updates it when the row comes round again. A closed pull request the committee wants back is reopened, or replaced by a new one on the same branch; earlier ones stay listed in Agentic status. Agentic status (Green) says where it is, and Staging review opens the preview's what-changed page. Before the preview is staged, the agent writes the change set's Disposition (change set) on the Agent tab: one line per feedback item, starting from the people's Blue Disposition, after an optional Overall statement; the sheet shows it in Disposition (agent) and flags any item without a disposition, or one that differs from the people's. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/contributor-feedback.bpmn#Task_EditInPullRequest . Flows to Task_PoInject, so the round-trip QA runs again over the corrected text — "edit the translation and re-run QA", which is what the adjudication step has always offered and what this process could not do. A userTask, not a service task: this is the one step here where a person edits content, and the lane's actor is the reviewer who just adjudicated. Hard: a failure blocks the PR. SHARDED since bean dlqu (drawn as one task, deliberately: a multi-instance marker would add a BPMN term to every instance's UML overview, about 75 generated files, for a picture this sentence already gives): the suite runs as three e2e-shard jobs (E2E_SHARD=i/3, one Playwright worker per core in each), and each shard is its own required check, so a shard that failed, was cancelled or never ran is a red check of its own. Until bean 5p4m (issue #2456) an e2e job carried one check name for the three and completed the task only when every instance succeeded; it was ~1 s of work behind a runner request that waited minutes, and was removed. Measured before the split: playwright test alone was 4m33s of a 5m16s job, the workflow's slowest once bun test ran in parallel. The BPMN-render and .bat-wrapper checks run in shard 1 only, so they are asked once. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/code-quality-gates.bpmn#Task_E2E . Three things come from it and none may be guessed. (1) Which subset strategies the source supports — supportsSubset(). (2) Whether a subset stands on its own: when subsetIsSelfContained is false (mathlib), the request is closed over its dependencies here, and every gate after this one is asked about the CLOSURE, because a subset that omits what its members depend on is not a smaller corpus, it is one that does not build. (3) What enumerating the whole costs — enumerationCost(), which is undefined when the descriptor has no measured denominator; SIZE then refuses rather than estimates. A source with no descriptor is not an error here: it is an unknown, and SIZE refuses on it. The descriptor is CALLED here rather than restated. A broad question is answered from summaries and a specific one from chunks; a pipeline that picks once has answered every future question the same way. 9754287295af.content: Gate every slice: slice:sqlite:check candidate, extracted For every slice: build twice and require one sha256; read the row digest back from the file and require it to equal the digest computed from the source without SQLite; run an FTS5 phrase query for a known row; and audit the payloads with auditPayloadTree (deploy payloads as written, the kg slice's pointers against the committed payload tree). Gate results: restore / save candidate, extracted Component 2c. RESTORE: the result store (build/result-store/) and the CI cone records, by prefix — a WARM start: the cone (ci-cone.ts) then matches each stored entry exactly (fingerprint from cache:key --base, every recorded path state, every replayed git answer) and only an exact match is reported SKIPPED, never passed. A committer's local gate record is class (b): honoured on the critical path, then re-verified off it. SAVE: main only (class c for CI's records). Owner roles: the gate-reuse session (CI speed 8) and the committer-side session (CI speed 3). cache nodes: result-store, ci-cone, local-gate-records. A recommendation reaches the drafting step with its evidence attached, or with the gap recorded. This step has nothing to do for content that carries no recommendations -- a mathematics folio has none, and a figure redrawn from its own source adds none -- and the subprocess's first gateway (Gateway_RecommendationInPlay) ends it there at its own event, recording the answer, rather than satisfying the search vacuously. Hand new feedback to the row's agent; take over stalled rows candidate, extracted On every poll, changed or not, new Blue feedback goes verbatim to the agent working the row, and a stalled row is restarted or taken over. A row is stalled when its Blue cells changed, or Ready for agent turned Yes, more than 10 minutes ago and no Agent step was recorded since; or when its agent recorded no step for 2 hours. A stalled row's owning thread is asked once; with no answer within 10 minutes, or a thread that is done or stopped, the watcher takes the row over, or asks the coordinator for a new thread, and writes the new owner, the step and a link into Feedback (agent). Import hygiene (HARD) and advisories (WARN-ONLY) candidate, extracted FOUR QUESTIONS, ONE RUNNER — bean 7fu5. They were four jobs (lean-bare-import, python-imports, rust-wildcard, dependency-advisories), each about a second of work behind a ~13 s checkout and a runner request; measured on main run 37133247484 (2026-10-03), the run took 21.7 min while its longest job executed for 174 s, the rest waiting for runners. Now they are steps of the hygiene job, and every step after the first gate runs if: !cancelled(), so a red one masks none of the others — the om30 rule kept inside one job rather than by splitting it. (1) Lean, HARD: fail on any bare import Mathlib in content/**/*.lean; in this platform repo there is no content/, so the step prints SKIP and states that nothing was scanned. (2) Python, HARD: ruff F401 (unused) and F403 (wildcard) over the Python trees that exist, then the Python tests; an absent tree is dropped rather than passed to ruff, and an empty set says SKIP. (3) Dependency advisories, WARN-ONLY by the owner's ruling on bean j41m: is anything in the resolved tree KNOWN-VULNERABLE? The script exits 0 in every state and keeps them apart in its output; .github/dependabot.yml is the other half of that ruling and is not drawn here. (4) Rust wildcard imports, WARN-ONLY: report non-test use …::*; in tools/**/*.rs; continue-on-error, and therefore the job's LAST step, where it masks nothing. Re-pinning is the half that is easy to forget and is the reason this is a step rather than an absence: without it the same upstream change is detected as new on every cycle, and a contributor is asked the same settled question for ever. The record says the copy is deliberately divergent FROM a named revision, which is a different claim from being stale against an unknown one. Land each member candidate, extracted Once per member, in train order, at the SHA the train's gate set tested. merge-to-main.bpmn is where merging is a step with its own gate: it reads the head's evidence live (the train's green run is that evidence, and merge:guard re-evaluates it), establishes that the owner authorised THIS merge (explicitly, or by a standing ruling quoted verbatim with its date, e.g. 2026-10-01 "you may merge green PRs", which covers green heads only and only the queue as it stood), records the authorisation, merges pinned to the head, and then confirms main, re-pins downstream mounts and notes the bean. Until 2026-10-09 this was two steps here, Task_Release in the owner's lane bound to interaction-modality and Task_Land bound to prepare-merge; neither could refuse a merge, and neither said what happens when a repository has no CI. R1 still holds: what lands is exactly what CI tested. If main moved after the train's CI started, re-run rather than land. 47a22466b3dd.title: M
47a22466b3dd.content: Make sure every step is done candidate, extracted Following a harness's instructions once is not the same as every step being done. complete-initialization walks the steps the declarations name — FIRST the harness's JSON Schemas and JSON-LD at the IRIs they name, the primary step of initializing a Knowledge Graph harness; then declared directories, assets, the README and its sections, and the site that carries the documents — checks each, does what can be done, asks the person for what only they can do, and reports every step in its state. An agent may be dispatched to run it on its own: it needs nothing but that diagram and the declarations. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_CompleteInitialization . Make sure gh-pages exists and Pages serves it candidate, extracted Provisioning the target, owned by this process rather than by the publication step that calls it. Pages cannot serve a branch that does not exist, so in order: (1) an orphan gh-pages branch exists — git ls-remote --heads origin gh-pages; if absent, push a placeholder (index.html + .nojekyll); (2) Pages is on, Source = the gh-pages branch at / — gh api -X POST repos/<o>/<r>/pages -f source[branch]=gh-pages -f source[path]=/ when gh is signed in, otherwise the exact manual step (Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch → gh-pages, / (root)). Each half is done, not done, or could not be determined; never assumed. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_Provision . Make the change candidate, extracted The loop's only open-ended step. Everything around it is procedure; this is the work. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_Implement . Make the change candidate, extracted content-change-review-make.bpmn: scope the change, branch, edit content and logic, assess and absorb the downstream impact, and push. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Call_MakeChange . Make the change, check it and merge it candidate, extracted The second phase, drawn on its own page (public-comment-change.bpmn): an author edits the document as decided on a feature branch, the change set is reviewed on its staging preview, an independent QA gate checks the dispositions against the pull request, and each comment it answers is marked incorporated when it merges. A withdrawal still interrupts the comment while this runs. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/public-comment.bpmn#CallActivity_MakeChange . Make the PR ready candidate, extracted Its own work is done and its full tier is green as judged; it is marked ready by the queue rule (continual-progress, Pace the ready marking). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-request.bpmn#Sib_Ready . Make the value proposition and set next steps candidate, extracted DIIG Chapter 9. The case made to whoever pays, and what follows. Scaling up is a different method and a different publication — 9789241509510-eng, The MAPS Toolkit — which begins where this implementation ends. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/collab/processes/diig-investment-path.bpmn#A_ValueProposition . Map concepts to WHO Commons dictionary candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/collab/processes/content/SGAuthoring.DAKLifecycle.bpmn#Task_MapToCommons . The DAK's L2 content is l3-fhir-authoring's sourceModel; l2-dak-authoring, bound beside it, carries the WHO L2 → L3 ordering, which the generic skill does not name. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/L3/collab/processes/dak-l3-ig.bpmn#Task_MapL2 . It lists every site downstream in waves, so a site moves only after the layers it takes from have moved, and marks which sites are ready now. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/guideline-updates.bpmn#Task_MapCone . Map the current state and confirm bottlenecks candidate, extracted DIIG Chapter 3.1. Determine the health programme processes to target, map their workflows, identify and confirm bottlenecks. Then 3.2, a root cause analysis. This is where DIIG builds on CRDM, and it says so: "This process builds on the Public Health Informatics Institute's Collaborative Requirements Development Methodology (CRDM)". Its three areas of concentration are business process analysis, business process redesign and requirements definition — two of which name diagrams this platform already executes. They are parallel tracks, not a composite: pick one per decision and name it. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/collab/processes/diig-investment-path.bpmn#A_MapCurrentState . Map to ICD-11, SNOMED CT, LOINC candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/collab/processes/content/SGAuthoring.DAKLifecycle.bpmn#Task_MapToStandards .
