A palette per kind would be three spellings of "accent colour", free to disagree about what an accent IS. Where the source is SILENT on a role, say so and mark the value a choice rather than dressing an invention as a measurement. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/ingest-theme.bpmn#Task_MapRoles . Mark confirmed items withdrawn (keep bytes) candidate, extracted The record gets a withdrawn state; its bitstreams stay addressable, because a citation to them may exist. BPMN activities of who-iris · source who-iris/processes/iris-cdn-reconcile.bpmn#Task_MarkWithdrawn . Mark every copy answered candidate, extracted Chat copies keep their text: the question struck through and "[Edit: <letter> chosen by <who>, <time>]" added. Cards closed with the chosen option. The sheet's "Decision needed" block replaced by the decision and who made it. Withdrawn or superseded hand-backs marked the same way, with the reason. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#D_MarkAnswered . Mark incorporated when the change set merges candidate, extracted public-comment incorporate, naming the branch, PR and staging URL; done by the folio's workflow when the PR that closes a change-set issue merges. A PR closed unmerged moves nothing. Ready for merge is set only once the QA gate has passed for the PR's head commit; set earlier, the agent does not merge until it passes. The change set's Dispositions blurb, as it stands when Ready for merge is set to Yes, is the summary that closes its issue. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/public-comment-change.bpmn#Task_Incorporate . Mark it skip on the queue candidate, extracted Record on the queue file that the bean is held elsewhere, and by whom, so no other drainer takes it next. The bean itself is not touched: closing or noting on someone else's bean is how a sibling loses work it had not finished reporting. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/bean-drain.bpmn#Drain_Skip . Mark the record superseded or retired candidate, extracted Never delete (git rm) a superseded or retired requirement. When superseding req:<old-slug>, set status: superseded and supersededBy: req:<new-slug> on docs/requirements/<old-slug>.md. When retiring, set status: retired and document the retirement reason and authorising issue in prose. Update any RequirementSet (docs/requirements/*.set.json) so approved/accepted sets hold only in-force members. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/requirements-filing.bpmn#A_UpdateLifecycle . Materialise the part candidate, extracted The ONLY way bytes arrive. Purpose first, then the five gates — size, restrictions, copyright, retention, source loss — then fetch with fixity, or stay referenced with the refusing gate's basis recorded. Both ends of that subprocess return here and the walk continues: one part refused is not the subscription refused. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Call_Materialize . Materialize remote content (the five gates) candidate, extracted The shared subprocess. It resolves the request against the source descriptor, then asks size, restrictions, copyright, retention and source loss, and either fetches with fixity or leaves the content referenced. This process does not restate any of that; it waits for the outcome. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/sample-import.bpmn#Call_Materialize . Measure the cutover: separation:cutover:check candidate, extracted Run bun run cat separation:cutover:check --site in the SEPARATED repository (Tool separation-cutover-check). Six conditions, each decided by an existing gate and none assumed: every declared layer mounted at its pin; every path a declaration names resolves (check:declaration-resolution — directories, assets, visualisers, needs); no wiring still names the monorepo (livesAt, a submodule, a reusable workflow, a path into the old checkout); no import or reference against the layer order; and the site builds from the mounts alone. A finding inside a mounted layer is upstream's and is listed, not counted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-cutover.bpmn#Task_CutoverCheck . Measure the signals candidate, extracted Files and bytes per layer, clone cost (bun run cat health), gate time, merge contention, the candidate's cohesion and cut (kg:detangle), wrong-direction edges, and the would-be tools package's import cone. Recorded in the work context; none alone is a trigger. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Measure . Mechanical checks, both viewports candidate, extracted Tool wireframe-check renders every candidate at a web and a mobile viewport. It fails on horizontal overflow at mobile width, on placeholder text, and on a missing viewport, and writes screenshots and a script entry per criterion. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#D_Check . Merge and publish candidate, extracted content-change-review-publish.bpmn: merge on the owner's explicit confirmation, then remove the staging preview, rebuild main and watch it. An unmerged change keeps its preview. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Call_Publish . Merge each member onto the base candidate, extracted merge-base.bpmn once per member, in order, --no-regen; then ONE bun run cat regen over the result. Tool: merge:train. Always onto the current base, never a cached one (R5). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-train.bpmn#Call_MergeMembers . Merge into each locale candidate, extracted Merge each refreshed template into every locale's catalogue: new strings arrive empty, changed ones fuzzy, and obsolete ones are kept as #~ entries, never deleted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_MergeLocales . Merge it through merge:guard candidate, extracted A workflow PR, or a PR in a repository with no train, merges directly. A workflow PR needs no approval beyond the batch card (owner ruling, 2026-11-07, card Workflow PRs, A). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-manager-watch.bpmn#Task_Direct . Merge main in, regenerate, fix mechanical gates candidate, extracted Merge commits only; never a force-push. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_AgentFix . Merge manager watch candidate, extracted The elected session holds the merge steward lane and runs its loop until it hands over or the lane lapses. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-request.bpmn#Sib_CallWatch . Merge restored and rebuilt records candidate, extracted Combine the restored per-artefact records with the cone's freshly rendered ones into one complete set, so the meta-index rebuild that follows has every artefact's record and never re-derives one. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge the base in, without committing candidate, extracted git merge --no-ff --no-commit origin/main on a clean tree (untracked files refuse too, so the final stage cannot sweep in a scratch file). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-base.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge the one source PR to main candidate, extracted All the templates in one PR to main, merged before any locale starts, so every translator branches from the same main. Once it has merged, its branch receives nothing more: a later fix to the source is a new PR. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/multi-locale-translation.bpmn#Task_ML_SourcePR . Merge the PR candidate, extracted Merge the layer's PR to main, then confirm the template checks pass on main. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_Merge . Merge the pull request candidate, extracted The agent merges the row's pull request, and Agentic status says merged. The change set's Dispositions blurb, as it stands when Ready for merge is set to Yes, is the summary: it goes into the merge, and closes the change set's issue. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/contributor-feedback.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge the re-pin with its decided revisions candidate, extracted The re-pin merges when its checks are green and every decision it needs is recorded. Its pull request cites the decisions, which become the release notes for this site's update. Merge train candidate, extracted Add the merge-train label instead of merging; the train lands the batch with one CI run. Their words are quoted verbatim in the record, so the answer is given in the conversation or on the PR, not inferred from tone. Merge, on explicit confirmation candidate, extracted The owner says "merge it", and only then is the branch merged. Merge to main triggers: 1. the main site rebuilds with the changes; 2. the staging preview's cleanup runs; 3. the review comments committed on the feature branch land on main, as the review record. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review-publish.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge, pinned to the evaluated head candidate, extracted Through merge:guard <pr> --merge --session <id> where the repository has it; elsewhere with the merge call pinned to the head SHA, so GitHub refuses if the head moved. Merge commit unless the repository or owner says otherwise. Never delete the branch. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_Merge . Mirror it to the feedback channel candidate, extracted Review sheet: the "Decision needed" block in the row's agent column, Agentic status Needs you (the document layer's review-sheet-script skill). Issue or PR: a comment. An extra copy, never instead of the discussion. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#S_Mirror . Monitor, and use data effectively candidate, extracted DIIG Chapter 8. Establish a logic model, plan the monitoring and evaluation, establish a culture of data use, and manage adaptively — using the data to optimize the interventions rather than only to report on them. The full treatment of this chapter is a separate publication in this library, 9789241511766-eng, Monitoring and Evaluating Digital Health Interventions. It is a parallel track, not a sub-step: do not blend the two. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/collab/processes/diig-investment-path.bpmn#A_MonitorAndUseData . Mount each layer at its declared path candidate, extracted Sparse checkout of the declaration and the chosen directories, copied to the mount path (by default the layer's home path, so relative imports and sibling discovery hold). Never onto tracked bytes; never onto a directory no lock says this mount made; never over edits to a previous mount — those are left untouched and reported. A replay of the lock tries the index's layers cache ref first (refs/cat/layers/<key>, then refs/cat/layers/main): one shallow fetch, every byte verified against the lock, and any layer that does not verify is fetched from its own repository. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-dependency.bpmn#Task_MountInstances . Mount the branch tip at the declared path candidate, extracted A branch source keyed by tip: branch-store mount --id <dir-id> writes the tip's files at the declared path, so every reader finds the directory where it always was; push splices edits back onto the tip, never forcing, and a same-file race is a conflict. The branch's NAME is the declaring directory's storage (or source) — a branch no declaration names is refused rather than guessed. A commit-keyed branch is read per commit through its own store (qa-store), not mounted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-subgraph.bpmn#Task_MountBranchTip . Mount the remote tree at its pin candidate, extracted A remote source: another repository's tree at a full 40-character commit. bun run cat mount:remote lays it down at the declared path and locks its tree digest; it is never written back, because the bytes are somebody else's at somebody else's pin. Usually reached through a source.remote layer in the root index.config.json (legacy: remoteMounts), which expands a whole harness and its closure — Process_MountDependency. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-subgraph.bpmn#Task_MountRemotePin . Move harness output about it to the host candidate, extracted QA verdicts, translation templates, the exported graph and the glossary ledger are harness output ABOUT the graph: they live with the harness (kgQaHomeFor, translationsHomeFor). The content keeps only what its own checks need; the leak test's pending list is empty. The one exception is a separated layer that declares a qa directory of its own with storage: its verdicts are its own repository's, published to that repository's qa-reports branch (step 10), and read by a host at the commit it pins. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-prepare.bpmn#Task_Hosted . Move into library/<bib-slug>/ candidate, extracted The folder name IS the bibliography citation key, so a citation and a directory are the same string. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#Task_Promote . Move it into its repositories candidate, extracted Create the repositories, drain, seed, consume additively, release, and check every identifier dereferences. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Call_Move . Move it into its repository candidate, extracted Create the repository, drain, copy the staged contents in, re-point the declaration, verify a fresh clone, then consume, release and check every identifier dereferences. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Call_Move . Move the entry's ref and re-cache the declaration candidate, extracted Only after every held part has been through the refresh. Moving the ref first would make the records of parts not yet refreshed describe a commit the entry no longer names. The cached declaration is replaced so the review that follows shows what the NEW pin offers, including subgraphs that did not exist at the old one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_RePin . Move the pin and open the PR candidate, extracted The pin literal moves in the one file upstream-pins.json declares, and the PR body says what the version range changed in RENDERED output — the evidence, not just the verdict. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#A_ApplyPin . MVP: build the candidate on a staging branch candidate, extracted An MVP is a DEPLOYED BUILD, not a description of one. The pin is moved on a branch and feature-staging.yml publishes it under branches/<branch-slug>/, so the reviewer looks at the artefact rather than at a screenshot — the same argument the merge discipline makes about rendered work. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#Task_Mvp .

f6925faa815c.title: N
f6925faa815c.content: Name the subject and the level candidate, extracted One sentence naming WHAT is being analysed and at WHICH level — individual, organisational, national, international. The source requires this before anything is listed: "the classification of a variable also depends on the purpose of the practice", and the criteria for assigning a variable to a quadrant "may be more difficult to clarify if the methodology is not used for a company but for a country". It also bounds the known limitation that SWOT "is rarely deployed at lower than the organization level", where one scan drives strategy for units its factors do not hold equally for. Naming the level does not remove that risk; it makes it visible in the record. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_FrameSubject . Name the substrate, pin a full commit SHA candidate, extracted owner/repo and a 40-character commit SHA — never a branch, never an abbreviated SHA. The schema refuses anything else (SubscriptionSchema.ref), and this step exists so the refusal is met while choosing rather than at commit time. A tag replaces the SHA only once the substrate publishes releases. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Pin . bd22b61a7110.content: OCR to ocr/page-*.txt candidate, extracted Each page is read in the document's languages (--lang-hint, from dc.language.iso), narrowed to the script the page shows. A page Tesseract is unsure of (mean word confidence under 70) is read again with each other installed script added, and the most confident read is kept: a French article's Arabic abstract, or the Latin URLs in an Arabic document's references. A document ingested this way keeps its text in ocr/ and only a stub in sections/, which the documented sections/ grep cannot see. That asymmetry is why the corpus-grep checklist has a fourth tier. The run also records WHICH SOFTWARE made the pages, in ocr/run-context.json: a folio-run-context/v1 (cat-harness schemas/run-context.ts, the record test runs and QA reports use for the same question), naming the OCR engine, the rasteriser and each language model with its version and the sha256 of the bytes that ran. Two OCRs of one scan can read differently ("Manual" and "Manval"), and without it neither could be told from the other or reproduced. Options analysis accept · revise · discard candidate, extracted On the edge out of Task_ReviewFindings and before Task_RecordDecision: the findings are the evidence, so the options can only be weighed once they exist, and after Task_RecordDecision the decision is already written down. Not between Gateway_EditorDecision and Task_RecordDecision: Flow_21b runs Task_RecordDecision -> Gateway_EditorDecision, so the gateway reads a decision already recorded. In the Agent lane: the subprocess records that the options were WEIGHED (its own decision-audit note), and Task_RecordDecision in Lane_Editor records WHAT WAS CHOSEN. The analyst is not the decider. (CallActivity_Evidence is in Lane_Editor because the author performs the retrieval.) On the trigger: A_Frame opens the subprocess on opening-brief's trigger — irreversibility and surprise — and leaving there is a correct outcome. A spelling fix that reached Task_ReviewFindings with one mechanical finding exits immediately; a revise-or-discard on a block other content depends on does not. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis adopt · hold · decline candidate, extracted On the single edge into PM_Decide, and deliberately not earlier: the MVP build and its gates are HOW the options' costs are measured, so an analysis before Task_Mvp would weigh alternatives against no evidence. Everything the decider needs exists by the time the reviewer has finished and the fixable findings are fixed. In the Agent lane, because this step produces the analysis and does not make the decision — PM_Decide is a userTask whose lane admits person only, and putting the analysis in the agent's lane is what keeps that separation legible rather than implied. A subprocess that decided would be a second accepting party. Reached through the loop as well as straight through: SF_UA_8 re-enters at A_Impact, so a run where the reviewer found something fixable arrives here a second time with different evidence. That is a genuine re-analysis and its op="note" appends rather than deduping, which is the behaviour wanted — a second note records that the options were weighed again against changed inputs. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to absorb the impact candidate, extracted On the edge OUT of Task_AssessImpact and before Task_CommitPush, because the impact assessment is the evidence the options are weighed against. An analysis before it would compare ways of absorbing a downstream effect nobody has measured yet; one after the commit would be a rationalisation of a choice already pushed. Not between Task_AssessImpact and Task_ReviewImpact: those are in different processes with no sequence flow between them; the assessment reaches the committee through Task_CompareBeforeAfter. In the Agent lane, matching upstream-version-adoption: this step produces the options and their trade-offs, and GW_Approved in the committee review is where a decision is taken. On the trigger: reaching this call is not the same as running the whole of it. Process_OptionsAnalysis opens with A_Frame, whose trigger is opening-brief's — irreversibility and surprise, not size — and leaving at that first activity is a correct outcome rather than a skipped step. A copy-edit exits immediately; a logic change that moves an indicator (from Task_EditLogic) does not. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to implement candidate, extracted On the single edge from Start_Process_CRDM_Deliver into A_Implement, so the approach is chosen before any code exists. By Phase 6 the needs, requirements and data model are signed off, which is exactly the evidence an options analysis needs and the reason it belongs here rather than earlier: at Call_Needs there is nothing to weigh, and after A_Implement the choice has been made in code. The three loop-backs into A_Implement — _5 (increment rejected), _7 (MVP not ready), _13 (feedback translated) — deliberately BYPASS this call. Routing them through it would run the subprocess on every iteration of the inner loop, which is the ceremony this design refuses: a gate invoked on every pass stops being read. An iteration reworks an approach already chosen; if the APPROACH is what is wrong, that is not a loop iteration and it belongs to the calling step in crdm-requirements.bpmn. Contrast upstream-version-adoption, where the loop DOES re-enter the analysis. There the loop-back returns to A_Impact, which re-gathers the evidence, so the second pass weighs genuinely different inputs. Here the loop returns to implementation with the evidence unchanged. A_Implement carries a note on the bean (its claim is the OPEN that Process_CRDM calls first); this step carries no bean op, because Process_OptionsAnalysis ends with its own decision-audit note on the bean the caller claimed. 500a3b326382.title: P
500a3b326382.content: P1.1 · Agree the terms candidate, extracted The parties agree the purpose, the datasets, the period, the conditions and duties, which trust anchors each side accepts, and the legal basis the sharing rests on (consent, treatment, public-health law or a research waiver). This sets what the text must say; it is a negotiation between people. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_AgreeTerms . P1.2 · Write the legal text candidate, extracted Write the agreement as a document folio: one normative statement per clause the parties must keep, through normative-statements. The text says which governs if it and a machine-readable form disagree (suggested: the text). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_WriteText . P1.2a · Record the legal basis candidate, extracted The text states the legal basis the parties agreed in P1.1 as a normative statement: consent, treatment, public-health law, or a research waiver. Consent rule 1: only an agreement whose legal basis is consent carries the odrl:obtainConsent duty; treatment, public-health law and research waivers do not rest on consent. The gateway that follows, the ODRL and the reviewers all read the basis from this statement. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_RecordLegalBasis . P1.2b · Draft the plain summary candidate, extracted Consent-based only. Write a plain-language summary of the agreement in the same document folio: what it lets the recipient do with the person's data, in words the person can read. Consent rule 3: every agreement that needs consent publishes this summary, hashed with the agreement (P2.2a), and the summary is what the person consents to. It is reviewed, rendered and versioned with the text. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_PlainSummary . P1.3 · Derive the ODRL 2.2 Agreement candidate, extracted Computable only. One assigner and one assignee (ODRL 2.2 §2.1.3), permissions and prohibitions with target assets (§2.2), constraints (§2.5.1) and duties (§2.6.3), written as JSON-LD. Purposes from HL7 PurposeOfUse. Consent rule 1: the Agreement carries the odrl:obtainConsent duty only when the legal basis recorded in P1.2a is consent. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_DeriveOdrl . P1.4 · Check the ODRL against the text candidate, extracted Computable only. A person checks that the ODRL says what the text says, and signs it off. A program can check the ODRL is well formed; it cannot check that it matches the text. The check includes the consent duty: present when the legal basis is consent, absent otherwise (consent rule 1). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_CheckOdrl . P1.5 · Split public terms from private annexes candidate, extracted Split the agreement into a public template and private annexes (security controls, named staff). Only the hash of a private annex is ever published. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_SplitAnnexes . P1.6 · Sign candidate, extracted The signatories sign: wet ink, or an electronic signature under national law. Technically a detached JWS (RFC 7515) or CMS (RFC 5652); PAdES for a signed PDF needs the owner's approval. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Sign . P14.2 · Decide what happens to existing grants candidate, extracted Existing grants keep citing the old hash. The parties decide, per agreement: they stay valid until expiry, or they are revoked and reissued against the new version (in smart-trust). The old version stays readable. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_DecideGrants . P14.3 · New consent needed candidate, extracted The amendment widens use, so a Consent citing the old version's URL and hash does not cover the new version (consent rule 2). Record on the bean, and in the new version's text, that new consent is needed; the new version gets its own plain-language summary (P1.2b). Asking each person again is the trust layer's. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_NewConsentNeeded . P14.5 · Set the status to ended candidate, extracted Set the life-cycle status of the agreement's DCAT 3 record (DCAT 3 §6.4.30). The published versions stay readable at their URLs. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_SetStatus . P2.1 · Assign version and fixed URL candidate, extracted Each signed version gets its own immutable URL (for example /dsa/42/v3). A 'latest' URL may exist; nothing cites it. 4823c4028600.title: Q
4823c4028600.content: QA gate: check dispositions against the people and the pull request candidate, extracted Before Ready for merge. Reads: the change set's Disposition (change set), each comment's Blue Disposition on Review Public Comments, the PR's diff at its head commit, and the staging QA report. Checks that every comment number has one disposition; that each agrees with the people's Blue Disposition; that each Accepted or Partially accepted comment has its change in the diff, and a Not accepted, Noted, Deferred, Duplicate or Out of scope one has none; that the diff changes nothing no disposition accounts for; and that the QA report for the staged commit has no failing gate. Writes: QA gate (change set), first line "Passed <head sha>: …" or "Failed <head sha>: <why>", and QA report (change set), the report's link. The sheet shows both under Staging review; a pass for an older commit reads as stale. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/public-comment-change.bpmn#Task_QaGate . QA gate: check dispositions and PR candidate, extracted Reads: the change set's Disposition (change set), the people's Blue Disposition and feedback, the pull request's diff at its head commit, and the staging QA report. Checks that every feedback item has one disposition; that each agrees with the people's Blue Disposition; that each Accepted or Partially accepted item has the change in the diff, and a Not accepted, Noted, Duplicate or Out of scope item has none; that the diff changes nothing no disposition accounts for; and that the QA report for the staged commit has no failing gate. Writes: QA gate (change set) on the Agent tab, first line "Passed <head sha>: …" or "Failed <head sha>: <why>", and QA report (change set), the report's link. The sheet shows the gate under Staging review; a pass for an older commit reads as stale. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. QA working copy, built once (NOT A GATE) candidate, extracted Bean jtfk, issue #2456. bun run qa:working-copy (bean 72a8) — the bootstrap kg-export, then every declared QA writer — used to run INSIDE each job that reads the QA tree, and qa-publish ran the same writers again: nine builds of one tree from one commit, measured at 2,284 of 4,714 runner-seconds (48 %) on run 37659324493. Now the qa-working-copy job builds it once and uploads everything the build changed as an artifact with a sha256 manifest; each reader downloads it, checks the manifest against the hash this job reported and every restored file against the manifest, and only then judges. An artifact rather than a cache, because a cache key built from less than the real inputs serves stale data; an artifact is per run and exact. It judges nothing, so it is not a gate and does not reach GW_Join; a failed build fails every reader at its first step (they run if: !cancelled()), never a skip. Drawn feeding GW_Readers, the four tasks that wait for it; within them typescript-static and gates-standalone read no QA tree and do not wait, and qa-publish waits for it as well as for Task_RepositoryGates. bd6a03228c1f.title: Glossary: BPMN activities, R–Z
bd6a03228c1f.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 653 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 56 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 255 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-sci 14 (SKOS) · smart-base 161 (SKOS) · who-iris 34 (SKOS). One of 3 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 446 terms and is 361 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 1140 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 1140 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 446 shown . R S T U V W

AND THE NEW FIXITY IS RECORDED IN THE SAME CHANGE. This step rewrites bytes that a materialization record describes, so leaving the old digest behind would make a CORRECT run of this process fail check:materialized-fixity as a mismatch — the gate reading "somebody edited held content without saying so" about the one process whose job is to replace it. This is the publication exception, stated as a rule rather than as a carve-out, because a list of permitted writers goes stale when a writer is added. The exception is NOT "these actors may skip the rule"; it is "say what you did". A writer that updates the digest alongside the bytes passes, and the record then describes what is actually there. READ OFF THAT IG rather than from general knowledge: a GDHCN trustlist distributes KEY MATERIAL as W3C DID documents, and says nothing about what you wrap your bytes in — the health-certificate envelope is a separate specification in the same IG, and a document package is not a health certificate. So what is settled is where a verifier GETS THE KEY, not what it verifies. A portal that can fetch the bytes but not reach the trustlist cannot verify, which is unknown and not a failure — air-gapped is a declared deployment value, so that case is answered rather than assumed away. Still OPEN and unread: the rotation and revocation model, and whether a document-package signature can be expressed for a GDHCN-aware verifier at all. Two schemes with different properties remain to choose between, and the trustlist does not choose between them. A PACKAGE signature over the manifest verifies the SET — nothing added, removed or altered — and must be reissued whenever any file changes. A PER-ASSET signature verifies one file independently, which is what an edge cache serving one asset can actually check, and it cannot detect a removal because there is nothing left to verify. They compose; composing them is the safer and more expensive default, and it is the deployment's choice rather than the pipeline's. What an agent doing ingestion work does here is DRAIN a few: bun run cat summaries:next -- --n K hands it the next K blocks with their text, it writes a short summary of each in its own words, and bun run cat summaries:record writes them into library/<bib-slug>/summaries.json as drafts naming the agent and its model. The block itself stays verbatim and ingested. A library can ask for a summary in more than one language (the six UN languages for a WHO publications library, owner 2026-11-11): the English draft, one in the document's own language read from the source, and translations of the English into the rest, each its own narrative in the block's slot. Method: skill l1-document-ingestion, "Summarising prose blocks". ADVISORY, never a gate: this step does not hold up Task_Citeable, and check:l1-complete reports the backlog (block-summaries) without failing on it. Confirming or rejecting a draft is a person's act, in bun run cat narratives. 2a9914750fe5.title: Glossary: BPMN activities, A–D
2a9914750fe5.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 653 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 56 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 255 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-sci 14 (SKOS) · smart-base 161 (SKOS) · who-iris 34 (SKOS). One of 3 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 381 terms and is 306 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 1140 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 1140 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 381 shown . 0–9 A B C D

0d46e348f476.content: Abort, restore the tree, list what was refused candidate, extracted git merge --abort. Each refused path is listed with its pattern's reason, or "no declared pattern". An unprompted offer is accepted as it stands — do not make somebody follow a process to hand over what they already have. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Accept . A row the pass could not finish stays changed and is picked up on the next poll. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/review-log-watch.bpmn#Task_Accept . Accept, or send back candidate, extracted The editor's lane, kept separate on purpose: the reviewer who judged the change is not the position that accepts it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Task_EditorDecides . Accessibility: measure, do not assert candidate, extracted Contrast COMPUTED against the real ground, including the worst case a backdrop can present; a non-colour channel wherever colour carries meaning (SC 1.4.1); an accessible name on every region; keyboard and focus order. An automated pass is necessary and not sufficient — axe accepts a non-empty placeholder as an accessible name, and a CSS selector that matches nothing raises no error at all. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#A_Accessibility . Descend into Process_CriterionAdjudication, which runs the shared adjudication and then one of its three outcomes: the checker's finding stands, the criterion is scoped, or a dispensation is granted with its reason. The checker's entry is kept beneath the verdict rather than overwritten (requirement R4 of issue #1042). Adjudicate the conflict candidate, extracted A human or agentic decision, never a merge rule. Which side wins depends on why the local edit was made, and a process that picked automatically would be choosing without the one fact that decides it. Adjudicate the criterion disagreement candidate, extracted The shared judgement — entry condition, untainted dispatch, person-or-agent restriction — asked with THIS question's permitted answers. cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes sits here rather than on A_Adjudicate inside it because the answers depend on what was asked, and the gateway below is what acts on them: the engine refuses a mismatch between the two. A branch frozen for public comment is dispatched with build_type: full instead. Skill feature-staging, section Build types. A PREVIEW REBUILDS ONLY ITS DEPENDENCY CONE (owner cards Q-CONE-1 C and Q-CONE-2 B, 2026-11-01): main's writer records say what each derive:publish writer and each step of the QA working copy READ. A writer or QA step whose recorded reads all match is not run, and main's outputs for it are put back. Every other one runs. QA is not left out of a preview, only narrowed to what the change can reach. Inside a preview's QA build, skill:register also leaves to derive:publish the two pages that derive:publish builds anyway and that no later QA step reads (skills:docs and lsi:viz), so they are built once. Build the entry candidate, extracted First the working copy is produced (qa:refresh, bean 3hk4): while the checkout still tracks test/results/, the commit's own copy is the record and nothing runs; once it does not, every declared QA writer runs into the empty tree, because the gates are in judge mode and wrote nothing a publish could carry. A refresh that leaves a writer failed, a family empty or a file unclaimed is INCOMPLETE: the job goes red and qa:publish --completeness refuses, so a partial tree is never stored as the commit's record — the "Not stored" outcome, reached before any push. Then it hashes the working copy of every declared qa directory (<instance>/test/results/**, byte-identical to the checkout's layout) into a tree through a private index, and writes manifest.json (qa-reports-manifest/v1): inputs, producers, verdict counts and the gates' result. Identical JSON is the same blob, so an unchanged family costs nothing to store again. Its git objects live in a private bare repository, never in the checkout's own store. A stale cache is first rebuilt incrementally (IncrementalBuildCli), falling back to a full AstExportCli build with -tx; a force run, a pre-export caller, or a missing or cannot-tell cache always builds in full, and a release needs a full build. The caller's optional pre-export overlay command runs before a full build; the inputs it changed are put back and the AST is recorded against the clean commit's input digest (ig-ast.ts source-inputs). Two checks: that the site build stages each one at its address, and that each address answers. A 404 is not published; a 403 or no answer from here could not be determined. Check the selected methodology's evidence base candidate, extracted Before applying a methodology, establish that the thing being applied is what it claims to be. A methodology is adopted because it is somebody else's named, external work; this step checks that the origin it cites resolves to a source in a declared library, and reads the methodology-evidence QA sidecar for it. WHY THE CHECK IS HERE AND NOT AT ADOPTION. Adoption happens once; selection happens every time a decision is made. A source that was reachable when the methodology was adopted can stop being so, and a methodology adopted before this axis existed was never checked at all. Measured 2026-09-22: six methodologies cited an origin and NONE had that source in any library, so every selection made until then rested on an unverifiable citation. WHAT A GAP DOES AND DOES NOT DO. A missing source does NOT block the decision, and this step has no branch that stops the process — that would make a documentation gap into an outage, and the owner decides whether an unbacked methodology may still be used. It does two things: it runs literature-search to try to close the gap, and it puts the evidence state into the record A_Record writes, so a reader can tell a decision made on a verified method from one made on a citation nobody could follow. The third state is the one that matters. "Source ingested", "source located but unreachable from here" and "no source found" are three different facts, and literature-search exists largely to stop the middle one being reported as the last. Discuss it with the person candidate, extracted Bootstrap's human-agent discussion, given the composed question. Its Ask ONE question step is where this harness's delivery rule applies: Post the whole composed question as ordinary chat text BEFORE any card. This is the copy that survives: a card, once answered, shows only the chosen option, and a dismissed card shows nothing. Never "see the card", never a request for a typed reply such as "1y 2n". A type that disagrees is reported, never changed. A relationship between two linked elements that no term lists is reported, and removed with --prune along with the lines that draw it. No box or line is moved. Without --write it only reports; --check fails when anything would change. --seed goes the other way once, and only from an ingested model held under library/ (--from): an authored model is never a source of the glossary. Check a review log and its repository's issues for changes candidate, extracted The mechanical check a review-log watcher runs on every poll. Given a drafting sheet's Contributor Feedback values and the folio repository, it reads the repository's open and closed issues (leaving out pull requests, issues labelled no-sheet and, with --author, issues someone else opened) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human) and Change Set (human)) with the last check's. Unchanged: it prints {"status":"unchanged"} and exits 0. Changed: it exits 10 and lists what changed (issue opened, updated or closed; a cell's old and new text), the Contributor Feedback rows to append, one per issue that no row's Issue cell links yet (Title the issue's title, the first Contributor Feedback column @login (#N): first paragraph, Issue the issue's URL; a closed issue's row marked closed), and closedRows, the rows linking a closed issue, which the watcher hides with their text struck through. A read with no Issue column (a public-comment log's Review Change Sets) tracks only issues labelled change-set unless --label says otherwise, and appends no rows: each open issue is reported as an issue-unlinked change instead. It writes no sheet and no issue: the watcher appends the rows and does the agent pass. With --accept it stores the new state for the next poll to compare against. df257caa1c31.content: Extracted candidates are minted from this repository’s own assets and are not, by themselves, checked against any vocabulary. check:term-mapping asks whether each already exists as a concept somebody is authoritative for — SKOS for what a term MEANS, FHIR for a clinical code’s operational semantics — and the two are separate questions with separate answers. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 5006 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 5006 | 0 | — | . a1de0be3a616.title: bibliography/ page: as-is intent
a1de0be3a616.content: Covers: the bibliography visualiser folio-assistant-core declares in folio-assistant-core.json (renderedBy: bibliography-page, coversKinds: [references, catalogue], subgraphs: directory), routed at en/folio-assistant-core/bibliography/. It is generated by folio-assistant-core/scripts/bibliography-page.ts (bun run cat bibliography:page, the bibliography-page Tool) and gated by check:bibliography. Candidate: as-is.html, the index page, with the page of one sub-graph drawn below it. Checked at web 1280 and mobile 390. Who it is for: a reader or an author of a folio who wants a reference the knowledge graph holds, whether a folio cites it (a references node) or a catalogue holds it (a Dublin Core record). It works like the glossary viewer, limited by path to sub-graphs and single assets. What they need to do: find a reference, read its citation, see where it came from and whether the library holds it, and export the whole list, one sub-graph’s list, or one reference, in the format their tool reads. What it must show, as the generator writes it: . On the index (<route>/): . | what the page holds: references directories’ folio-reference/v1 nodes and catalogue directories’ Dublin Core records, as one list; | the export of every reference shown: BibTeX, CSL-JSON, RIS and Dublin Core / BIBO JSON-LD, as files beside the page; | a “By sub-graph” line linking each declared directory’s page, with its count; | a filter box with a live count; | every page of the route keeps out of the site’s search index (search_exclude: true), so the site’s search data does not carry the bibliography; | a list longer than 500 references is not written out: the page says how many it holds, links the sub-graphs (on the index) or the documents (on a sub-graph’s page) whose pages list them, lists only the few no page below lists, and keeps its exports; in place of the list it offers a search box over the route’s static, sharded search index (<route>/search/, bibliography-search.ts): every word of the query must begin a word of the reference, results show their count by sub-graph and by decade (each a filter) and link the page that lists each reference; | per reference, in an ordered list: the citation (up to three authors then “et al.”, year, title, container, volume, issue, pages, publisher); its key as a link to its own page (<route>/<sub-graph>/<key>/, a slash address with no #), which a click opens in the right-side panel; its provenance (catalogue or authored); its DOI or URL; its ISBN; the source file it was read from; where the library holds it; and its own export as BibTeX, RIS and CSL-JSON downloads. A reference EXTRACTED from a document’s reference list (provenance: extracted) has no page of its own: its key opens its detail in the side panel from the page that lists it, and its export is in that detail. | . On each reference’s own page (<route>/<sub-graph>/<key>/; for a library item, its asset page): every bibliographic field, every place the work can be read (its URL, DOI, arXiv page, repository and pinned copy, DSpace handles), where it sits in the KG, and its export. An entry with no title shows its citation as the source printed it. On each sub-graph’s page (<route>/<sub-graph>/): the directory, its layer and kind, a link back to all references, the same four exports over that directory alone, and the filter and list.

e424a19e7d50.title: glossary/ page: as-is intent
e424a19e7d50.content: Covers: the glossary visualiser folio-assistant-core declares in folio-assistant-core.json (renderedBy: glossary-page, coversKinds: [glossary], alias glossary), routed at en/folio-assistant-core/glossary/, and the per-asset-type pages beside it. All are generated by folio-assistant-core/scripts/glossary-page.ts (bun run cat glossary:page) and gated by check:glossary. Candidates: as-is.html is the index, and as-is-type-page.html is one asset type’s page (Schema fields, the largest). Both are checked at web 1280 and mobile 390. Who it is for: anyone who meets a word in a folio and wants to know what it means: a reader, an author choosing a term, or an agent binding a term to an external concept. What they need to do: find a term fast, read its definition, see its code, see which external concept it matches, and tell an authored definition from a candidate extracted from a knowledge-graph asset. What it must show: . On the index (glossary/): . | the counts by state (authored, candidate extracted, could-not-extract); | a Pages table: this page and one row per asset type (skills, Tools, BPMN activities, DMN decisions, schema fields), each linked, with its term count and size; | the index’s own size and its budget (64 KB), and the per-type budget (1 MB); | the authored terms, with a filter box and live count, and an A–Z letter bar; | per term: the label, the code (notation) when the label and source do not already say it, a status badge when not authored, the definition, the scheme, the term IRI for an authored term, the source as a link to the asset, and the external matches as links; | a Sources list: each scheme with its SKOS JSON-LD link, the swimlane ledgers (linked, never copied), and the external schemes referenced through remoteGraphs; | a table of the extracted schemes, layer by asset type, each column heading linked to that type’s page and each count linked to its SKOS; | schema.org DefinedTermSet JSON-LD for search engines, carrying the authored terms only. | . On each asset type’s page (glossary/<type>/): . | a link back to the index, and a sentence on what the terms are read from; | which layers contribute, each with its count and SKOS link; | the page’s size and its budget; | the filter box with a live count, the A–Z bar, and every term with the “candidate, extracted” badge. | . Every term is on exactly one page: authored on the index, extracted on its type’s. Authored terms are minted by the layer that owns their source, in its own namespace (cat-harness’s platform terms in cat-harness’s platform scheme; core’s in glossary), so the index lists each authored scheme with its owning layer. The swimlane index is linked as a source, not rendered a second time. An extracted term’s IRI is left to its scheme’s SKOS rather than printed on every row. A type page over its budget is split by the first letter of the label, on fixed ranges. glossary.test.ts pins that every term appears once across the pages, that each page is under its budget, and that the index links every type’s page; check:glossary fails a page over its budget.

1c118461f661.title: Все рабочие процессы в репозитории
1c118461f661.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR . Сколько всего файлов BPMN 2.0? На этой странице это число больше не указывается, и это исправление, а не уклонение от ответа. Предложение, с которого раньше начинался этот раздел, содержало число, и оно оказывалось неверным пять раз подряд — «шесть», затем «девятнадцать», затем «тридцать», затем «тридцать два, все в processes/», затем «тридцать девять» — каждое оставалось неверным достаточно долго, и каждый раз ошибку обнаруживал кто-то, кто случайно запускал ls. Последнее из этих значений расходилось с реальностью на шестнадцать, когда его наконец проверили: оно утверждало тридцать девять против пятидесяти пяти. Число в тексте — это утверждение; производный индекс — это доказательство. Поэтому само число находится в производном индексе процессов, который генерируется из объявления командой bun run cat auto:docs, проверяется в CI и не может разойтись с диаграммами, которые он подсчитывает. Задача этой страницы — та половина информации, которую невозможно сгенерировать автоматически: для чего предназначен каждый процесс, в какой момент вы в нем окажетесь и какой из соседних процессов вам на самом деле нужен. Такое разделение является правилом навыка auto-docs, и эта страница — наглядный пример его применения: индекс показывает, что существует и что каждая диаграмма заявляет о себе; всё, что приведено ниже, сообщает то, что индекс структурно выразить не может. Диаграммы bootstrap намеренно вынесены за пределы этого индекса, и их отсутствие — это осознанный факт, а не упущение. bootstrap/workflows/ объявляется в bootstrap/bootstrap.json, а не в корневом репозитории, поскольку объявление их там снова переносит процесс bootstrap в опубликованный граф корня — что было намеренно удалено в #432 и до сих пор защищено тестом. Bean pve3 фиксирует этот выбор: обе половины bootstrap либо ни одной. Поэтому производный индекс охватывает то, что объявляет корень, а три диаграммы bootstrap вместо этого перечислены в таблице ниже. Каждая из них представляет собой настоящий документ BPMN 2.0 с поддержкой обмена диаграммами (diagram interchange) — откройте его в bpmn.io, Camunda Modeler или любом другом инструменте BPMN. Файлы SVG во всей документации генерируются из этих файлов командой bun run cat render:bpmn; никогда не редактируйте SVG вручную. Прежде всего остального — процесс, с которым человек сталкивается первым, и единственный, который выполняется, когда фолио еще не существует. В этой таблице до 20-09-2026 упоминался файл bootstrap/workflows/bootstrap.bpmn — файл, которого не существует, переименованный в initialize-harness.bpmn задолго до этого, — в то время как все три реальные диаграммы оставались неназванными. Висячая ссылка, скрывавшаяся за каталогом, который ничто не сканировало — именно то, для обнаружения чего и существует проверка not-indexed, но не могла поймать, поскольку каталог был невидим и для неё (bean 7u3g). Теперь строки указаны верно. Диаграммы по-прежнему невидимы для инструментов, и это сделано намеренно в ожидании решения: bootstrap/workflows/ объявлен в bootstrap/bootstrap.json, но не в корне, а объявление его там снова переносит процесс bootstrap в опубликованный граф корня — что было намеренно удалено в #432 и до сих пор контролируется тестом. Bean pve3 фиксирует этот выбор: обе половины bootstrap либо ни одной. | Диаграмма | На какой вопрос отвечает | . | bootstrap/workflows/bootstrap.bpmn | Агента направили на репозиторий, и ему ничего не известно. Является ли это уже экземпляром — загрузить его — или нет, и в таком случае чем он должен стать? Единственный ввод — ссылка на экземпляр; тип harness, граф знаний и голос считываются из объявления этого экземпляра. Единственный процесс в bootstrap, который ЗАПУСКАЕТ актор — агент начальной загрузки (Bootstrapping Agent), прочитавший bootstrap/README.md, находится на начальном событии и ему больше неоткуда начать. Это решения того, кто запросил harness, поэтому никакие инструкции их не генерируют. Он находится в bootstrap, а не в harness, поскольку bootstrap не может импортировать harness, так что логгер, определенный выше по течению (upstream), был бы недоступен актору, который больше всего нуждается в протоколировании своих действий | . | getting-started.bpmn | Кто-то сказал: «создай фолио». Шлюз намерений (intent gateway) здесь вычисляется, а не выбирается вручную: decisions/folio-intent.dmn возвращает ветку, и ask — один из возможных исходов, что и делает вопрос обязательным, а не просто вежливостью. См. Начало работы. Не зависящие от контента — эти три процесса применимы к любому фолио, причем внешние ссылаются на внутренние как на действия-вызовы (call activities), благодаря чему каждый процесс описывается один раз и используется повторно: . | Уровень | Диаграмма | На какой вопрос отвечает | . | 1 | Жизненный цикл контента — content-lifecycle.bpmn | Один цикл фолио, от планирования до вывода из эксплуатации (plan → retire) | . | 2 | Черновик → публикация — draft-to-publication.bpmn | Как корпус становится официально опубликованным фолио | . | 3 | Редактирование и валидация HCI — editing-hci-validation.bpmn | Что происходит с одним предлагаемым изменением в одном блоке контента | . Специфичные для типов контента — как создается конкретный вид фолио. Они располагаются внутри шага Draft the block edit уровня 3 и сопровождаются соответствующими руководствами: . | Диаграмма | Тип контента | Где описано | . | authoring-a-document.bpmn | Документы и нормативные руководства | Написание документа | . | authoring-a-paper.bpmn | Научные статьи и книги | Написание статьи | . | l2-dak-authoring.bpmn | Комплект цифровой адаптации ВОЗ (WHO SMART Guidelines DAK, L2) | Создание WHO SMART DAK | . | l3-fhir-pipeline.bpmn | Руководство по внедрению ВОЗ (WHO SMART Implementation Guide, L3) | Создание WHO SMART IG | . | ig-incremental-build.bpmn | WHO SMART IG (L3) — дорожка сборки, инкрементальная по конусу зависимостей (предложено) | Инкрементальная сборка · обзор | . Как он превращается в согласованные требования и кто утверждает результат? Внешний процесс; его шесть фаз — это действия-вызовы (call activities), описанные ниже. См. Ветка вычисляется с помощью decisions/signing-route.dmn, считывающего охват (reach) актора и то, настроена ли конечная точка; незаявленный охват интерпретируется как unknown и направляет к человеку, поскольку шлюз, предположивший «подключено», создал бы неподписанный отчет, выглядящий как подписанный | . | actor-role-administration.bpmn | Изменение того, кто что может делать: добавление актора и объявление его типа, открытие или закрытие роли, предоставление или отзыв разрешения, вывод актора из эксплуатации без удаления — затем аудит.
